text.p: As far as business travelers are concerned, it's the coming and going part of renting a car that counts, not necessarily how much it costs.

That comes through in a recent survey from J.D. Power and Associates that found that more than half of a customer's satisfaction with a rental car deal is based on how well the pick-up and drop-off process goes.
Price and value, on the other hand, accounted for less than 20 percent of what went into a customer's impression.

Given the contractural arrangements with suppliers often imposed by corporations on business travelers, the information might not seem very pertinent to car rental companies who may assume they are dealing with customers who have no choice.

But Paula Sonkin, client account director at the marketing and information firm, says Power's research shows a "good percentage" of business travelers still have a choice of which car rental company to use.
They may have to stay within a certain price range, she said, but "it's interesting how many are personally involved ..." in deciding who gets their business.

This is the second year that J.D. Power has surveyed car rental customers. Sonkin said the relative weight given such things as the ease and efficiency of the pick-up and return in overall satisfaction has not changed much in the two polls.
The survey involved seven major U.S. car rental companies doing business at airport locations. More than 4,000 questionnaires were distributed to a mix of business and leisure customers.
The survey found that Hertz was rated No. 1 in customer satisfaction followed by National and Avis.
On another car rental front drivers with a black mark or two on their records may find they've been denied permission to rent a car.

States that make driving records available to online services through which car rental companies can make checks are Alabama, Arizona, California, Connecticut, Florida, Idaho, Kansas, Maryland, Minnesota, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina and Virginia, as well as Washington D.C.

That information comes from the 1997 edition of "Best Travel Deals," a handy paperback, pocket-sized book packed with travel information published by Consumer Reports and seling for $8.99 in the United States.

Its section on car rentals says that drivers can be denied a rental for three moving violations or two accidents over a three-year period, or for one instance of drunk driving or other serious offence.
The book, which covers a wide range of travel topics, is available at bookstores or by calling 800-500-9760.
